Thus Socrates procured his daemon; and Iamblichus has left particular writings and treatises on it, to teach the means of having such spirits <sup class="mk" data-key="r">r</sup>. Great ravings and dangerous illusions, which St Augustine has learnedly and amply recounted <sup class="mk" data-key="ſ">ſ</sup>: for they are nothing but the juggleries, enchantments and trickeries of that great father of lies, Satan, who very often transfigures himself into an Angel of light to deceive men <sup class="mk" data-key="t">t</sup>. english.html: I remember that oaks struck from heaven foretold it (De coelo tactas memini praedicere quercus).

The example of it is also at hand in Tanaquil, wife of Tarquinius Priscus, fifth King of the Romans, who, seeing a flame of fire surround the head of a poor child called Servius Tullius, foretold thereby that he would be King of Rome <sup class="mk" data-key="x">x</sup>. Cicero in a certain place shows that, by the discipline of the Etruscans, if from a fire there came a double flame, or the flame at its point divided in two, that presaged quarrels and dissensions <sup class="mk" data-key="y">y</sup>. Under Pyromancy may justly be comprised Capnomancy, which is a kind of divination made by the smoke of the fire: for if it turns in a circle it signifies one thing; if it goes crosswise, or bends, or else stretches straight upward, it presages another <sup class="mk" data-key="z">z</sup>. Aeromancy is divination by the air, as by the flight and song of birds at liberty, by rains, tempests and unaccustomed storms. Thus when it rained stones in the March of Ancona (which the Latins always called Picenum), there was signified the defeat and carnage that Hannibal made of the Romans in Italy <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>. Hydromancy is made by inspection, and the invocation of spirits, in water <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>: as when a young child (of whom Marcus Varro speaks) saw in the water Mercury, who recited in a hundred and fifty verses all that came to pass in the war of Mithridates <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>. De Cœlo tactas, memini prædicere quercus.
L'exemple auſſi en eſt preſent de Tanaquil, femme de
Tarquinius Priſcus, cinquieſme Roy des Romains, la-
quelle voyant vne flamme de feu enuironner la teſte
d'vn pauure enfant appellé Seruius Tullus, predit par
là, qu'il ſeroit Roy de Rome {x}. Ciceron en quelque lieu,
demonſtre que par la diſcipline des Hetruſques, ſi d'vn
feu ſortoit double flamme, ou la flãme ſur la pointe, ſe
diuiſoit en deux: cela preſageoit noiſes & diſſentions {y}.
Soubz la Pyromance, peut eſtre iuſtement comprinſe
la Capnomance, qui eſt vne eſpece de diuination qui ſe
fait par la fumee du feu: car ſi elle ſe tourne en rond, ſi-

bien ſ'eſtend droite contremont, en preſage vne autre {z}.
Aeromance, eſt diuination par l'air, comme par le vol &
chant des oyſeaux, eſtans en liberté, par pluyes, tour-
mentes & orages inaccouſtumez. Ainſi quand il pleut
